result.title: Same Answer, Different Future: Matched Predictions Do Not Imply Matched Belief Updating in Language Models
result.summary: Language models can produce similar probabilistic predictions after observing outcomes, reading summaries, receiving instructions, or undergoing activation interventions. Whether these routes induce equivalent belief states remains unclear: agreement in current predictions does not establish how a model will respond to subsequent evidence. We investigate this distinction in a Bernoulli inference task with an analytic Bayesian reference. Across three open-weight language models, we prepare states through four textual routes and two activation-level interventions, measure both next-outcome continuations and explicit probabilistic estimates, and append identical new evidence from each prepared state. We quantify the persistence of the initial belief through its effective evidence weight, the number of new observations it is worth. We find that the format of evidence decides which readouts express its content: outcome sequences primarily affect continuations, whereas summaries and stated rates primarily affect explicit estimates. Moreover, effective weights differ substantially across routes, with summaries receiving weights that scale weakly with their stated observation counts and elicitation questions changing inferred weights by orders of magnitude. In a one-shot steering setting, an intervention that reproduces a natural record's immediate prediction loses most of its effect under subsequent evidence. These results show that agreement in current readouts is insufficient to establish equivalence in belief updating: how a belief is acquired and how it is read jointly determine its subsequent dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Bernoulli 推断任务中，用四种文本路径和两种激活干预构造模型状态，并以「有效证据权重」量化初始信念的持续性，发现当前预测一致并不代表后续证据更新一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 「相同预测≠相同信念状态」的配对读出与有效证据权重，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否真正承载视觉证据，以及同答案不同内部状态下的更新差异，但需迁移到多模态并检验估计有效性。
